title: The Good Little Witch
summary: Every one of Aura's spells comes out back to front, and her cat Bigotes never knows who they're going to end up helping.

scenes.text:
In a crooked house at the edge of the woods lived a little witch called Aura.

She had a hat that was far too big, a stripy scarf and a black cat called Bigotes.

Aura wanted very, very much to do magic. The trouble was that all her spells came out back to front.

If she wanted to make Bigotes fly, the stool flew instead. If she wanted a nice hot chocolate, she got a chocolate ice cream. If she wanted to tidy her room, her socks went and hid under the bed.

Bigotes was used to it. Every time Aura raised her wand, he jumped off the stool, just in case.

"Miaow," he would say. Which in cat language means: here we go again.

One morning, Aura went down to the village with Bigotes.

It was raining, and in the square stood Doña Remedios, looking sadly at her washing on the line. It had been hanging there for three days, and it never got dry.

"I'll help," said Aura, and she raised her wand. "Let the rain stop!"

But the spell came out back to front. The rain didn't stop falling…

It started going up.

All the drops turned round and flew back up to the clouds, as if someone were calling them from the sky. Zing!

The village children ran out into the street to watch. The drops floated slowly upwards, shining, and slipped in under their umbrellas.

And Doña Remedios's washing was dry in no time at all.

In the afternoon, in the meadow, they found Nico crying under a very tall tree.

His red kite was tangled in the very highest branch.

"Don't worry," said Aura. "Kite, come down!"

And of course, the spell came out back to front.

The kite didn't come down. Nico went up.

Slowly, floating like a soap bubble, Nico rose through the air to the highest branch. He grabbed his kite. And he floated down again, very gently, until he landed on the grass.

He stood there for a second with his mouth open. And then he burst into laughter.

"Again! Again!"

That night, Aura sat by her cauldron, with her hat drooping over her nose.

"Bigotes," she sighed, "nothing ever goes right for me. I'm the worst witch in the world."

Bigotes climbed into her lap and gave her hand a gentle head-bump.

Just then, there was a knock at the door.

Aura opened it. And there stood Doña Remedios with a basket of bread, and Nico with his kite. And behind them, the village children, every one of them holding something: a flower, a drawing, a biscuit.

"We've come to say thank you," said Doña Remedios. "My washing has never been so dry. And the children haven't stopped talking about the rain that went up."

"And I flew!" said Nico. "I flew!"

Aura didn't know what to say. So she did the only thing she knew how to do.

She went out into the garden, raised her wand and said:

"Let everything be calm and quiet!"

And of course, the spell came out back to front.

Out of the tip of her wand burst sparks. Pink, blue, yellow and green, swirling up and painting the sky with whirls and stars and moons of every colour.

The whole village clapped.

Aura laughed so much that her hat fell off. And Bigotes, from his stool, gave her the look of a cat who had known all along.

Her magic wasn't wrong. It was just hers.
